title: Coordinate Converter: DD, DMS, Minutes and More
description: Convert coordinate pairs between decimal degrees, DMS and degrees-minutes with the Coordinate Converter — paste a pair, switch formats. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, Times Square is 40.7580, −73.9855 in decimals, 40°45′28.8″N 73°59′07.8″W in DMS, and 40°45.480′N 73°59.130′W in degrees-minutes — one point, three dresses, all converted here.
quick_answer: The Coordinate Converter takes a coordinate pair and switches it between the common human and machine formats — decimal degrees, degrees-minutes-seconds, and degrees with decimal minutes. Paste the pair, read every format at once, and copy the one your chart, form or software actually wants.

Decimal: 40.7580, −73.9855. DMS: 40°45′28.8″N, 73°59′07.8″W. Degrees-minutes: 40°45.480′N, 73°59.130′W. The minus sign and the W are the same fact in two dialects.

faq: Which datum does it use?
WGS84 — conversions change the format, never the datum. A point in another datum needs a datum transformation first, which format conversion is not.
Which datum do these coordinate tools use?
WGS84 across this site's coordinate family, this converter included.
Do more decimal places always mean better accuracy?
No — format dress does not add knowledge. Six decimals from a two-decimal source is costume, and the precision tools here quantify the honest grain.
Can I copy the result into GIS software?
Yes — decimal output pastes directly; DMS strings paste into tools that parse them, with hemisphere letters as the safe form.
Hemisphere letters or signs?
Both are produced; use letters with DMS/DDM and signs with decimals, one convention per value — the sign trap example on this page shows why.
Batch conversion?
One pair at a time here — lists belong to spreadsheet formulas or GIS, with this page as the spot-checker of their output.
It rejected my input.
Separators and symbols vary; the Coordinate Parser loosens messy strings into clean values first, then conversion proceeds.
Radians included?
The degrees-radians lane has its own converter for the pure angle case; pairs in radians convert through the same subdivision arithmetic.
Zero and pole edge cases?
0,0 and the poles convert mechanically — formats survive where geography gets philosophical.
Which format should I store?
Signed decimal degrees, full precision, WGS84 noted. Every other format is one conversion away; originals in any other dress invite transcription archaeology.
Minutes can exceed 60 in my input?
That signals degrees-minutes misread as DMS or a typo — the parser and detector pages help untangle which.
